data.text: Time-constrained virtual tour optimization seeks an optimal path that covers the maximum number of points of interest within a time threshold (TTH) to avoid cybersickness. This threshold is the maximum duration of a VR tour allowed, as even minimum-time paths can cause cybersickness if they exceed it. Since there is no easy way to determine the TTH, which may depend on content and movement speed, it can be obtained from empirical studies or pre-existing results.
points: Time-constrained virtual tour optimization seeks an optimal path that covers the maximum number of points of interest within a time threshold (TTH).
The time threshold (TTH) is the maximum duration of a VR tour allowed to avoid cybersickness.
A tour covering all vertices in minimum time may still cause cybersickness if it exceeds the time threshold.
Time thresholds can be obtained from empirical studies or pre-existing results.

data.text: When planning a tour within a time threshold, visiting every point of interest is not mandatory. Nodes are assigned importance values to help determine which ones to cover, where the total importance of a path is the sum of these individual values. The objective is to find a path that maximizes total importance while respecting the time threshold.
points: Visiting every point of interest is not mandatory when planning a tour within a time threshold.
Nodes are assigned importance values to help determine which ones to cover.
The total importance of a path is the sum of the individual importance values of all nodes in that path.
The objective is to find a path that maximizes total importance while staying within the time threshold.

data.text: Each node in the virtual reality path optimization model has an importance and a waiting time, which is the maximum time a user requires to inspect or interact with an object. The total waiting time for a path is the sum of the individual waiting times at each node. The goal is to maximize total importance while ensuring that the path's total completion time, including waiting times, remains within a time threshold.
points: Each node has an importance and a waiting time, which is the maximum time a user requires to inspect or interact with an object.
The total waiting time for a path is the sum of the individual waiting times at each node.
The optimization problem maximizes total importance while ensuring the path's total completion time, including waiting times, is less than or equal to a time threshold.

data.text: The Vehicle Routing Problem with Profit (VRPP) is a model that maximizes the importance of visited nodes within a time constraint. VRPP solvers can be used to find the optimal path that maximizes total importance within a given time threshold. These solvers help visit as many important points of interest as possible while keeping user exposure below a threshold beyond which cybersickness may occur.
points: The Vehicle Routing Problem with Profit (VRPP) maximizes the importance of visited nodes within a time constraint.
VRPP solvers can find the optimal path that maximizes total importance within a time threshold.
These solvers help visit important points of interest while keeping user exposure below a threshold beyond which cybersickness may occur.

data.text: The algorithm takes an original graph G with vertex importance and waiting times as input. It aims to find an optimal path that maximizes importance while staying under a time threshold. The graph is transformed into a complete graph and then into a final graph G'' weighted by travel times. A VRPP solver processes G'' to compute an optimal path, which is then modified to replace hypothetical edges with shortest paths from the original graph.
points: The algorithm takes an original graph G with vertex importance and waiting times as input.
It aims to find an optimal path that maximizes importance while staying under a time threshold.
The graph is transformed into a complete graph and then into a final graph G'' weighted by travel times.
A VRPP solver processes G'' to compute the optimal path P_opt.
The final path is modified by replacing hypothetical edges with shortest paths from the original graph.
